Items.Authors: Olivier Absil, Gilles Orban de Xivry, Prashant Pathak, Abhirami S. Raghu, Benjamin Courtney-Barrer, Roy van Boekel, Thomas Bertram, Markus Feldt, Matthew A. Kenworthy, Bernhard Brandl
Items.Title: Maximising mid-infrared high-contrast performance on ELT/METIS despite water vapour turbulence
Items.Abstract: The Mid-infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) will be equipped with a SCAO system delivering Strehl ratios around 99% in the N band (8-13µm). Yet, the actual wavefront quality seen by the METIS coronagraphic modules will be significantly affected by water vapour seeing. We analyse two years of VLTI/GRAVITY fringe tracker archives to assess the variability of differential water vapour column density at milli-second timescales on ELT scales. Our analysis suggests that water vapour seeing will add a median wavefront error of about 175 nm RMS at N band. If not corrected, this effect will degrade the achievable sensitivity limits in terms of contrast by more than 2 magnitudes. To mitigate this effect, we plan to deploy a focal-plane wavefront sensing and control algorithm based on an asymmetric pupil concept using a deep learning approach. We describe the expected performance of this secondary wavefront control loop, and its consequences on the METIS high-contrast performance.

Items.Authors: Lukas Rimmele, André Fehlmann, Isabelle Scholl
Items.Title: Mechanical design of resolver positioned cryogenic filter wheels
Items.Abstract: The Cryogenic Near Infrared Spectropolarimeter (Cryo-NIRSP) at the National Science Foundation’s Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) operates four filter and slit wheels on optical benches stabilized at 60 K. Because the slits lie at the focal plane, they must be positioned with high precision and repeatability. The instrument therefore relies on accurate wheel position feedback to select among various slit and filter configurations. The previous design used limit switches to verify wheel positions, but thermal cycling and mechanical runout led to unreliable feedback. A new wheel assembly has been developed that incorporates a magnetic resolver directly coupled to each wheel, providing accurate and robust rotational feedback suitable for cryogenic operation. This paper outlines the mechanical considerations and design approaches used to integrate the resolver into a cryogenic environment to improve positioning accuracy, reliability, and overall instrument performance.

Items.Authors: Sebastian Rabien
Items.Title: Membrane space telescope: packaging and deployment
Items.Abstract: Membrane mirror technology offers the prospect for future extremely large space telescopes. Utilizing a thin parabolic membrane as primary mirror base, very low aerial weights can be achieved. The flexible nature of those mirrors allows to roll those up for launch un unwrap in orbit. In this paper we will show a proposed foldable structure that can be compactly stared with the mirror in a launcher and deployed in space. With a scaled prototype model, we illustrate the system’s compact stowage and deployment character.

Items.Authors: Mohammad N. Islam, Aditya Krishna Karigiri Madhusudhan, James Trudel, Jagdish Singh, Tayron Dueck, Gordon Lacy, Richard Hellyer, Brian Hoff
Items.Title: Metrology-based surface and alignment verification of the Canadian Hydrogen Observatory and Radio-transient Detector antennas
Items.Abstract: The Canadian Hydrogen Observatory for Radio-transient Detector (CHORD) is a next-generation radio array of 512 six‑meter composite antennas being built at the Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory in British Columbia. The shape of composite reflectors are dependent on many factors such as mold accuracy, process induced errors, temperature, fabrication technique, post-production operations, etc. Surface distortion and alignment errors require higher degree of repeatability to meet various science goals. This paper presents metrology and manufacturing results from over 50 antennas using laser tracker and photogrammetry data. Surface errors average 0.5 mm RMS and alignment accuracy is within 1 arcminute, confirming that the composite fabrication process meets CHORD’s demanding performance and scientific requirements.

Items.Authors: Silvio Di Rosa, Demetrio Magrin, Roberto Ragazzoni, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Matteo Aliverti, Andrea Baruffolo, Luigi Lessio, Marco Dima, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Mohamed Yahia Bournane, Davide Greggio, Alessandro Ballone, Federico Battaini, Maria Bergomi, Elena Carolo, Paolo Cerpelloni, Simonetta Chinellato, Stefano Ciroi, Simone Di Filippo, Jacopo Farinato, Tânia Sofia Gomes Machado, Luca Marafatto, Matteo Munari, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Marco Riva, Enrico Cappellaro, Paolo D'Avanzo, Piero Giubilato, Mario Salatti, Paolo Spanò, Valentina Viotto, Simone Zaggia
Items.Title: MezzoCielo: from the opto-mechanical design to the on-sky demonstrator
Items.Abstract: MezzoCielo (Italian word for “Half of the Sky”) aims to be a revolutionary optical system, combining a relatively large aperture with an extremely wide Field of View. The telescope is based upon the concept of a central monocentric lens, comprehending a dodecahedral frame filled with low refractive index-high transparency optical fluid. The seeing-limited performances are reached through the use of a large number of identical cameras, located on the focal surface of the central sphere.   In this work, we will describe the current status of the instrument, focusing upon the mechanical investigation of the monocentric structure, the optical design of the correcting cameras and the path towards the construction of a small-scale prototype. Possible strategies for handling the huge quantity of data coming from the single observation will be investigated as well.

Items.Authors: Andrea Tozzi
Items.Title: MICHELANGELO: a new high resolution spectrograph for 3-5 micron band
Items.Abstract: MICHELANGELO is a proposed high-dispersion infrared spectrograph for exoplanetary atmosphere characterization in the 3-5 μm range, providing high-resolution spectroscopy (R > 50,000) in the L and M bands. This wavelength region is rich in diagnostic molecular features from sulfur-, nitrogen- species, optimal for detecting cooler exoplanets. We present the conceptual design employing innovative germanium immersion grating technology to achieve simultaneous L-band (2.9-4.2 μm) and M-band (4.3-5.5 μm) coverage in a compact design. The configuration uses two independent cross-dispersed echelle spectrographs (70×40×40 cm per unit), enablingh sensitivity for direct imaging of spatially resolved young planets and emission spectroscopy of transiting exoplanets. The compact design suits 8-10m class telescopes with adaptive optics and future space missions. MICHELANGELO bridges current facilities and future ELT instrumentation, offering 4-8 times detection speed improvement.

Items.Authors: Miranda Eiben, Jón Guðmundsson, Rustam Balafendiev, Thomas Gascard
Items.Title: Millimeter and sub-millimeter characterization of polymers used for infrared filters in high-sensitivity cryogenic microwave telescopes
Items.Abstract: Infrared filters are an important transmissive optical component in millimeter receivers, as they reduce radiative loading on cold stages, thereby improving cryogenic performance. However, the complex optical properties of the materials commonly used for these filters are poorly characterized, particularly in-band and in the sub-millimeter regime. The absorption and scattering properties of these materials are becoming increasingly important for designing high-sensitivity millimeter instruments, as their loosely constrained properties are one of the greatest sources of uncertainty remaining in white noise modeling. We report the absorption in the millimeter and sub-millimeter regime of nylon 6, nylon 6/6, PTFE and polyethylene (both bulk HDPE and foam HDPE used in radio transparent filter stacks). Additionally, we report the relative power scattered out of the main beam by these materials from 90 to 330 GHz, measured in free space by a robot-enabled scanning vector network analyzer.

Items.Authors: Oleksandra Rebrysh, Lorenzo Merli, Alessandro Ballone, Valentina Viotto, Davide Greggio, Simone Di Filippo, Luca Marafatto, Sylvain Cetre, David Barr, Federico Battaini, Gabriele Umbriaco, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Elena Carolo, Tânia Sofia Gomes Machado, Remon van Gaalen, Silvio Di Rosa, Edoardo Bellone de Grecis, Mohamed Yahia Bournane
Items.Title: MiniMATTO: towards the practical implementation of the MATTO test bench
Items.Abstract: MiniMATTO is a predecessor of the MATTO (Multi-conjugate Adaptive Techniques Test Optics) bench, being developed at INAF-OAPd. Due to the complexity of MATTO, it is required to properly test hardware and software pipelines.     In this work, we present the optomechanical design of miniMATTO, a predecessor of MATTO. The bench will incorporate three NGS sources, two DMs, and three SLM-based WFSs operating in both focal plane and pupil plane regimes.     Additionally, we describe the first tests performed using miniMATTO bench. Those include MCAO closed loop control tests, using DAO4MATTO; synchronisation of hardware across turbulence injection, wavefront sensing, correction stages; accuracy of the WFS measurements with SLM simulated WFSs. Finally, we present the verification of the pipelines and calibration procedures, demonstrating the readiness for the integration and operation of the full MATTO test bench.

Items.Authors: Eleonora Barbavara, Giovanni Isopi, Alessandro Attoli, Elia Stefano Battistelli, Paolo de Bernardis, Federico Cacciotti, Giuseppe Carboni, Ettore Carretti, Daniele Ciccalotti, Fabio Columbro, Alessandro Coppolecchia, Angelo Cruciani, Giuseppe D'Alessandro, Marco De Petris, Federica Govoni, Adelaide Ladu, Luca Lamagna, Pasqualino Marongiu, Silvia Masi, Matteo Murgia, Alessandro Navarrini, Alessandro Novelli, Andrea Occhiuzzi, Andrea Orlati, Alessandro Paiella, Giorgio Pettinari, Francesco Piacentini, Mauro Pili, Tonino Pisanu, Sergio Poppi, Luca Schirru, Gian Paolo Vargiu, Sofia Ferazzoli
Items.Title: MISTRAL: optical alignment and beam optimization at the Sardinia Radio Telescope
Items.Abstract: The MIllimeter Sardinia radio Telescope Receiver based on Array of Lumped elements KIDs (MISTRAL) is a cryogenic W-band LEKID camera installed at the Gregorian focus of the 64-m fully steerable radio telescope Sardinia Radio Telescope (SRT), in Italy, in May 2023. MISTRAL will take advantage of its 12 arcseconds of angular resolution, a 4 arcminutes wide instantaneous field of view and its high sensitivity, to be one of the most competitive instrument to observe the mm-wave sky. In this contribution an overview of the technical commissioning will be given, detailing on the optical alignment of the SRT's mirror as well as the analysis done for the beam optization.

Items.Authors: Hanshin Lee, Brian L. Vattiat, Gary J. Hill, John M. Good, Casey Kyte, Joshua Oppor
Items.Title: Mix and match as you go: evaluation of the Beam Switch Module with production Integral Field Unit fiber cables for VIRUS2 instrument
Items.Abstract: Previously, we detailed the development of the Beam Switch Module (BSM) for the VIRUS2 instrument and its integration/alignment results. The BSM distills the beam switching functions that many traditional spectrographs accomplished inside the spectrograph themselves into an independent module outside the spectrographs, but at the same time adding a double beam scrambling and fiber switching functions, thereby making the instrument compact, modular, stable, and scalable. Inevitably, having a separate BSM means extra throughput loss due to additional components involved. Our BSM R&D effort so far has shown this “perceived” loss can in fact be minimal, and, in return, the instrument can potentially be adaptable to observing modes that would otherwise require new instruments. We constructed a production BSM (BSM3) with fully assembled VIRUS2 IFUs integrated/aligned to the BSM. We detail the integration and alignment process and compare its measured throughput against the expectations.

Items.Authors: Hiro Otsuka, Takanori Sakamoto, Yuta Kawakubo, Motoko Serino, Hsien-Chieh Shen, Ryota Kamimura, Shinpei Kubodera, Yuki Sato, Taiji Hayashi, Takumi Maeyama
Items.Title: Modeling of curvature deviations in micro-pore optics for 6U CubeSat mission SEAGULL
Items.Abstract: SEAGULL is a 6U CubeSat mission designed to search for electromagnetic counterparts of gravitational wave events. For its X-ray telescope, we plan to use micro-pore optics (MPOs) manufactured by Photonis Inc. Each MPOs have a nominal curvature radius of 600 mm. By arranging four MPOs in a 2 × 2 configuration on a common spherical surface, the telescope can achieve a wide field of view of 8 deg × 8 deg. However, the actual curvature of MPOs varies depending on the manufacturing process, and the curvature difference should affect the X-ray focusing performance. To evaluate the focusing performance of MPOs more precisely, we analyzed the focal positions of locally irradiated X-rays on a single MPO and developed a simulator that incorporates curvature deviations introduced during manufacturing. We report the focusing characteristics obtained using this geometry-based simulator and discuss challenges in assembling X-ray telescopes using multiple MPOs.

Items.Authors: Alessio Nuti, Yuri Evangelista, Francesco Ceraudo, Giovanni Della Casa, Ettore Del Monte, Giuseppe Dilillo, Marco Feroci, Edoardo Giancarli, Riccardo Campana, Mauro Fiorini, Giovanni Lombardi, Massimo Rapisarda, Ajay Sharma, Giuseppe Bertuccio, Filippo Mele, Yinhe Zhu, Marco Grassi, Piero Malcovati, Jacopo Giani, Marco Tambussi, Matias Antonelli, Alexandre Rachevski, Irina Rashevskaya, Gianluigi Zampa, Nicola Zampa, Evgeny Demenev, Giancarlo Pepponi, Francesco Ficorella, Nicola Zorzi, Francesca Esposito, Immacolata Donnarumma, Alessandro Turchi, Ugo Cortesi, Fabio D'Amico, Marco Gai, Andrea Argan
Items.Title: Modeling the thermo-elastic deformation effects of the LEM-X coded-mask camera
Items.Abstract: The Lunar Electromagnetic Monitor in X-rays (LEM-X) is a proposed all-sky X-ray observatory on the lunar surface, based on wide-field coded-aperture cameras. In this paper, we investigate the thermo-mechanical behavior of the camera, focusing on the alignment tolerances and thermo-elastic deformations of its two main elements, the coded mask with its supporting structure and the detector plane, based on large-area Silicon Drift Detectors. Using finite element models, we quantify the distortions induced by the lunar thermal conditions and we assess their impact on the imaging performance. Particular attention is given to variations in mask to detector alignment, deformation of the mask pattern, and focal plane flatness, which directly affect the source reconstruction accuracy of the instrument. The results provide key inputs for the camera design, guiding the choice of materials, thermal control solutions, and mechanical tolerances needed to guarantee the required optical performance.

Items.Authors: Paula Betancourt Esparza, Salvador Cuevas, Luis A. Martinez Vázquez, Leonardo Garcés García, Carolina Keiman, Luis C. Álvarez Nuñez, Beatriz Sánchez, Mamadou N'Diaye, Arthur Vigan
Items.Title: Molecular mapping with the FRIDA instrument using NVIDIA GPU-based parallel computing
Items.Abstract: FRIDA is the new near-infrared integral-field spectrograph (IFS) of the Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC), offering medium and high-resolution spectroscopy and unique Northern-hemisphere access to young stellar associations relevant for exoplanet studies. We present a method to obtain molecular mapping from FRIDA-like observations using IFS simulated data, applying large-scale cross-correlation between high-resolution FRIDA spectra and high-resolution molecular spectral references. Each analyzed IFS datacube is processed pixel by pixel using cross-correlation, producing molecular maps that reveal composition, spatial distribution, and kinematics. Due to the large data volumes involved, we developed a parallel-computing pipeline based on NVIDIA GPUs to significantly accelerate the analysis. Once FRIDA becomes operational, this pipeline will support high-resolution spectroscopic studies, especially for exoplanet atmospheric characterization.

Items.Authors: Kevin Luke, Myriam Rodrigues, Mathieu Puech, Nicholas Boardman, Vivienne Wild, Oscar A. Gonzalez, Michele Cirasuolo
Items.Title: MOONS1D: science simulator for MOONS at VLT
Items.Abstract: MOONS1D is a new one dimensional science simulator for Multi-Object Optical and Near-infrared Spectrograph (MOONS) at VLT. MOONS1D is a collection of python modules which enable simulation of spectra with astrophysical templates, instrument response of MOONS and atmospheric effects. Simulation is run by standard ESO configuration files and the output is modelled according to the data model of MOONS.

Items.Authors: Alfio Puglisi, Andrea Baruffolo, Giulio Capasso, Chiara Di Prospero, Salvatore Lampitelli, Salvatore Savarese, Amedeo Petrella, Danilo Selvestrel
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT : Design of the Soft Real-Time Computer
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. MORFEO includes twelve separate wavefront sensors, two internal post-focal deformable mirrors, and it must coordinate the operation of the ELT M4 deformable mirror and six laser launcher units. While the data flow between these devices is handled by a dedicated real-time core, the Soft Real-Time Computer plays a fundamental role in system coordination, optimization, and interfacing with the rest of the instrument, in addition handling of special features like M4 segmentation and data recording for engineering and scientific purposes. This paper describes the design choices made to handle this complexity, while remaining within the bounds of the ESO-provided RTC Toolkit as dictated by telescope harmonization strategies.

Items.Authors: Marco Bonaglia, tommaso lapucci, Edoardo Redaelli, Giorgio Pariani
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: LOR WFS module final design overview
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.   The Low-Order and Reference Wavefront Sensor (LOR WFS) Module is a critical subsystem, comprising three identical units to measure low-order aberrations from Natural Guide Stars (NGS) across an 80 arcsec technical field of view. The final design utilizes high-stiffness acquisition stages (AST) capable of 600 mm x 300 mm travel and incorporates an anti-collision system (ACS) to ensure safe operation. Each LOR WFS unit is equipped with a visible-band Reference (R) WFS and a J+H band Low-Order (LO) WFS, with the LO channel configurable as either a full-aperture sensor (including a LIFT option) or a 2x2 Shack-Hartmann sensor.   This paper gives an overview of the design and technical challenges of the subsystem at the time of the subsystem final design review.

Items.Authors: Benedetta Di Francesco, Ivan Di Antonio, Gianluca Di Rico, Fabio Di Nicola, Simone Benedetti, Angelo Valentini, Amico Di Cianno, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Elisa Portaluri, Fiorella Nusca, Mauro Dolci
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: test and verification steps towards the calibration unit final design
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. As in any complex system designed for ELT-class telescopes, MORFEO relies on the coordinated operations of its internal subsystems. Among these, the Calibration Unit (CU) is an opto-mechanical system which projects a set of sources on the telescope focal planes, allowing for calibrations and test procedures. After the Preliminary Design Review, the subsystem is now advancing through the Final Design Phase.  During the last period, the CU underwent extensive laboratory testing to verify compliance with key requirements and to validate its current design. In parallel with the test results, the electronic and software control architectures have been consolidated as well. This contribution summarizes the results of these activities towards a matured CU design.

Items.Authors: Wenli Xu, Walter Seifert, Gavin Dalton, Myriam Rodrigues, Ruben Sanchez-Janssen, Andreas Kelz, Ramon Navarro, Rick Romp
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: evolutions of the optical design for the VIS spectrograph
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is a Multi-Object Spectrograph for the 39-meter ESO ELT in Chile. The instrument allows for a multiplex of 140 in the visible and 180 in the near-infrared wavelength ranges. Its Integral Field Units offer parallel observation of eight extended objects. As an ELT second generation instrument its architecture has experienced several major evolutions in order to maximize the instrument efficiency and minimize the risk and budget.   The optical design of the VIS spectrograph has played an important role in those evolutions. In this paper the evolutions of the VIS optical design are summarized. The actual optical design covering 390-952nm simultaneously with a spectral resolution R > 4000 and for selected narrow wavebands with R > 18000 is presented in detail. The optimized instrument parameters have been taken fully into account to satisfy the multiplex requirement too. The dioptric cameras provide good image performance for both low and high resolution observing modes.

Items.Authors: David King
Items.Title: MOSAIC at the ELT: the optical design of the ground layer adaptive optics (GLAO) natural guide star systems
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object spectrograph and IFU instrument for the ESO ELT, currently in its design phase. The MOSAIC Ground Layer Adaptive Optics (GLAO) subsystem uses Laser Guide Star Systems (LGSS) and Natural Guide Star Systems (NGSS), each being Shack-Hartmann Wavefront Sensors (WFS). Light from the MOSAIC focal plane is passed to 4 GLAO boxes, each containing one LGSS and one NGSS. Common optics are shared between the LGSS and NGSS - a large focal reducing lens and dichroic to split the light between the two systems. The novel feature of the common optics are they reduce by a factor of 10 the focal planes of the laser guide star at the extreme distances and collimates the beam of the NGSS. A steering mirror at the NGSS pupil steers the field to the NGS WFS. The pupil is resized to match the ESO ALICE detector and the lenslet array is placed within the camera.  An additional metrology system in each GBOX also monitors relative motion between the GBOX and the MOSAIC focal plate.

Items.Authors: Yohko Tsuboi, Ryota Inoue, Rintaro Nishiyama, Ayaka Mitsubori, Takahiro Seguchi, Yoshitomo Maeda, Daiki Ishi, Tomokage Yoneyama, Wataru Buz Iwakiri
Items.Title: Multilayer crystal configuration of the Bragg-reflection X-ray spectropolarimeter ParaDAXAS for an extended energy range
Items.Abstract: Simultaneous X-ray spectroscopy and polarimetry are increasingly required to study high-energy astrophysical processes such as accretion flows near black holes and magnetic reconnection. However, conventional X-ray polarimeters cannot achieve both high energy resolution and a large modulation factor. We are developing ParaDAXAS, a Bragg-reflection optical system with curved crystals arranged on a rotated-paraboloid surface, aiming to obtain high-resolution dispersed spectra in a defocused setup together with high-sensitivity polarimetry.  We demonstrate energy-band extension using multilayer (multi-d) crystal stacking. By stacking crystals with different lattice spacings, such as Si, Ge, and C, multiple energies can satisfy the Bragg condition at the same incidence angle, enabling a wider reflective bandwidth without degrading polarization selectivity. Using a Si(111)/Si(100) stacked crystal, we confirmed increased total reflectivity over a broader energy range with an X-ray diffractome

Items.Authors: Anand Nagesh
Items.Title: Nano Observatory as a Service (NOaaS): a cloud-connected space and ground telescope network for real-time sky mapping and awareness
Items.Abstract: Nano Observatory as a Service (NOaaS) is a new way of monitoring the sky—using a fleet of small telescopes in space, combined with ground observatories and cloud computing, to deliver real-time insights about what is happening above Earth. Instead of relying only on large, expensive observatories, NOaaS uses multiple compact telescopes in low-Earth orbit working together as a virtual global observatory. The NOaaS approach is built on five key pillars:  1. Space-Based Sky Coverage All Day, All Night  2. Global Hybrid Sensing (Space + Ground)  3. Real-Time Cloud Processing  4. Autonomous Operations  5.Open Access and Subscription Model

Items.Authors: Kazuhiro Nakazawa, Keigo Okuma, Shin'ichiro Takeda, Yuta Nishimura, Moeka Baba, Yuto Kobayashi, Yuki Omiya, Atsuya Tanaka, Shin Watanabe, Tadayuki Takahashi, Naoki Ishida, Mitstunobi Onishi, Toshihiko Arai, Hiroki Yoneda, Masamune Saito, Jun Kataoka
Items.Title: Narrow field of view Si/CdTe Compton telescope with high aspect-ratio coded mask; miniSGI - verification in the 511 keV to 1.8 MeV band
Items.Abstract: Semiconductor Compton telescope (SCT) is a promising device to improve the MeV sensitivity gap. Based on ASTRO-H/SGD, which adopted a deep well-type active shield to limit its field-of-view (FoV) to ~10 deg combined with a Si/CdTe Compton telescope to further reduce background in orbit, we are developing miniSGI, to demonstrate sub-degree angular resolution in the MeV band. Even for SCT, angular resolution in 0.5-1 MeV is about 2-4 deg, not enough to resolve celestial sources in Galactic center. miniSGI has one layer of 0.5 mm thick 250 µm pitch DSSD and another layer of 2 mm thick CdTe-DSD, which provides angular-resolution measure of <3 deg in 356 keV in Compton reconstruction. It is surrounded by 20 mm thick BGOs and combined with a 5 mm thick 0.8 mm pitch Tungsten coded mask. Using miniSGI, we achieved 0.25 deg Compton reconstruction coded-mask combined imaging of 511 keV. We are also verifying electron-track reconstruction of 1.27 and 1.8 MeV line gamma-rays with the system.

Items.Authors: Helen E. Jermak, C. M. Gutiérrez, Javier de Cos, Iain A. Steele, Josue Barrera, João Bento, David Copley, Christopher Copperwheat, Marta Escriche, Adam Garner, Alejandra Goded, Francisco J. Hernández, David Heffernan, Cesar Lopez, Juan Francisco Márquez, Jonatan Martínez, Adrian McGrath, Chloé Miossec, Alberto Prieto Antúnez, César Quintana, Ali Ranjbar, César Rodríguez Pereira, Fernando Sánchez Lasheras, Robert J. Smith, Miguel Torres, Juan José Fernández-Valdivia, Horacio Rodríguez Delgado, Beth Garton, Sebastian Buntin, David Law, Richard Ashley
Items.Title: New Robotic Telescope progress report: status and updates
Items.Abstract: The New Robotic Telescope (NRT) is a next-generation, 4-m class fully autonomous facility designed to deliver rapid, efficient follow-up of time-domain astrophysical phenomena. Although progress toward first light has slowed due to funding constraints, the consortium has continued to advance both technical and programmatic work packages.     Here we present the development of the optical design review, telescope and enclosure optimisation, segment-extraction and actuation systems and focal-station prototyping. Details about mirror fabrication and science operations data centre (SOCDC) will also be included.     Preparatory observatory-level planning continues as partnership agreements are finalised, with the optimised dome and associated civil works awaiting updated costings. Taken together, these developments reflect steady technical progress and convergence toward a refined, cost-effective design that supports the NRT’s ambitious scientific and engineering mission.

Items.Authors: Ross Robinson, Wyatt Robinson, Kevin Kearney, Zoran Ninkov
Items.Title: New VIS-VUV radiometric calibration facility for space-based instrumentation at the Rochester Institute of Technology
Items.Abstract: The Laboratory for Advanced Instrumentation Research (LAIR) at Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) is developing a radiometric calibration facility focusing on expanding into VUV capabilities. The current configuration for 120nm-1100nm coverage has dual monochromators illuminated with Deuterium lamps. The monochromator for shorter wavelengths operates entirely under a vacuum. Initial example results from Teledyne e2V CIS120-LN low noise variant.

Items.Authors: Romain Laugier, Jonah T. Hansen, Philipp A. Huber, Felix A. Dannert, Jens Kammerer, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Denis Defrère, Loes W. Rutten, Jeremy P. Scott
Items.Title: NIFITS, the nulling interferometry data standard and its role in the community
Items.Abstract: So far, the nature of nulling interferometers has prevented the use of the OIFITS format used for classical beam-combiners. The new data format NIFITS, is on track for broad adoption not only by most nulling teams around the world (Asgard/NOTT, GLINT, LBTI, LIFE) but also by modelling tools such as OIModeller.  By including a high-fidelity parametric forward model of the instrument along with the data, it empowers the user to deploy the full extent of their reduction and modelling tools even when agnostic of the details of the instrument. To illustrate the power of NIFITS, we present some examples of results obtained during a hackathon held in August 2025.  This is leading to the consolidation of data reduction and interpretation algorithms shared horizontally between different projects and vertically from early concept evaluation phase to exploitation.

Items.Authors: Maria Bergomi, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Luca Marafatto, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Gabriele Umbriaco, Remon van Gaalen, Thomas M. Herbst, Marco Dima, Davide Greggio, Silvio Di Rosa, Florian Briegel, Lars Mohr, Jacopo Farinato, Roberto Ragazzoni, Valentina Viotto, Simone Antoniucci, Gianluca Li Causi, Fernando Pedichini, Roberto Piazzesi, Alessio Caratti o Garatti, Al Conrad, Fabrizio Massi, Sam Ragland
Items.Title: NirvanaVIS: the visible GLAO-assisted speckle holography imager for LBT approaching first light
Items.Abstract: NirvanaVIS is designed to leverage the wide-field, Ground-Layer Adaptive Optics (GLAO) correction provided by LINC-NIRVANA on the Large Binocular Telescope. Its primary goal is to extend high-resolution imaging into the visible band, retrieving images with a highly uniform PSF across the field.  Implemented on the LN bench, it employs speckle holography to achieve near-diffraction-limited imagery over 52 x 52 arcsec FoV, with a pixel-scale of 6.5 mas/pixel. This yields a spatial resolving power below 20 mas corresponding to a factor of three better than HST and two times better than JWST, enabling diverse science programs.  With the core hardware secured by the end of 2025, if approved for installation, the project is on track to achieve first light in early 2027.  This work presents the current status, AIV procedures and commissioning steps. We also detail final solutions for challenges related to the 8K Teledyne COSMOS camera interface to the telescope and the data management strategy.

Items.Authors: Sofia Savorgnano, Pete Barry, Chris Benson, Matt Bradford, Thomas Brien, Simon Doyle, Victor Gómez, Steve Hailey-Dunsheath, Jesús Hernández-Aguilar, José Luis Hernández-Rebollar, David Hughes, Elijah Kane, Kirit Karkare, Alex Lapuente, Ryan McGeehan, Raúl Naranjo-Romero, Andreas Papageorgiou, Joe Redford, Iván Rodríguez, Sam Rowe, David Sánchez-Argüelles, Annie Tan, Marcial Tapia, Jair Vega
Items.Title: Noise characterization of line intensity mapping observations with SuMaC at the LMT
Items.Abstract: The SuperSpec-MUSCAT Collaboration (SuMaC) combines the SuperSpec on-chip spectrometer with the MUSCAT camera on the LMT to enable millimeter-wave emission-line and Line Intensity Mapping (LIM) studies. We present a noise characterization of LIM-style scans from the Summer 2025 campaign using a 3-pixel SuperSpec array. Using observations of Abell 370 and the VIPERS field, we quantify atmospheric and instrumental noise, assess spatial and spectral correlations, and evaluate their impact on map sensitivity. We also test noise-decorrelation strategies to guide performance optimization and future SuperSpec upgrades.

Items.Authors: Maddalena Bugatti
Items.Title: Non-parametric PSF reconstruction and correction for accurate radial velocity measurements
Items.Abstract: Precise radial-velocity (RV) measurements at the m/s to cm/s level require an accurate knowledge of the spectrograph’s instrumental profile. Parametric PSF/LSF models often fail to capture asymmetries or chromatic variations, introducing systematic RV errors. I present a non-parametric method to reconstruct the LSF directly from laser frequency comb (LFC) calibration spectra. By modeling each comb mode with a flexible, data-driven representation, we recover the local LSF without assuming a functional form. The resulting LSF is used to deconvolve stellar spectra, removing instrumental broadening and revealing intrinsic line shapes. This approach improves profile fidelity, reduces RV biases from PSF variations, and offers a robust framework for tracking time-dependent instrumental behavior, enabling higher precision in exoplanet and stellar RV studies.

Items.Authors: James R. Tucker
Items.Title: Novel approach to deformable mirror (DM) actuation
Items.Abstract: A novel approach to deformable mirror (DM) actuation is presented that overcomes challenges common in current state-of-the-art approaches. DMs are typically actuated by voltage-driven means. The proposed DM utilizes discrete, radiantly heated, thermal expansion pistons as actuators. Multiple thermal expansion pistons sit between a thin mirror and a reaction structure, which also functions as a heatsink. There are "holes" below each piston, allowing radiant heat to be directed to the piston, inducing local thermal expansion. Heat is drained from the piston through physical connection to the reaction structure. The balance between heat input and dissipation rate controls the temperature of the piston, and thus its height. DM sensitivity, response, and recovery time can be tailored by material selection (CTE, specific heat, emissivity, and thermal conductivity) and geometry (thickness shape, and interface cross-section) to optimize performance for the desired application.

Items.Authors: Reston Nash, Rishi Pahuja, Jason Fucik
Items.Title: Novel optic retention strategy using a helical spring energizer
Items.Abstract: We present a novel lens mounting scheme that uses an off-the-shelf helical energizer spring to provide very high radial stiffness for the optic while allowing for relatively large differential thermal contraction between the optic and its cell material. This approach could lead to a general lens mounting strategy that is simple to design and build while being applicable for a variety of sizes and operating conditions.

Items.Authors: Noboru Ebizuka, Takayuki Okamoto, Takuya Hosobata, Masahiro Takeda, Yutaka Yamagata, Minoru Sasaki, Makio Nishimaki, Kazuya Yamamoto, Yukinobu Nishio, Masahiro Konishi, Kazuya Matsubayashi, Kosuke Kushibiki, Hidenori Takahashi, Kentaro Motohara
Items.Title: Novel transmission gratings with large angular dispersion, high efficiency and wide spectral bandwidth II
Items.Abstract: We are developing several types of novel gratings, including a volume binary (VB) grating, trapezoid grating, reflector facet transmission (RFT) grating and prism array for a grism.　 The VB grating provides a larger angular dispersion and higher diffraction efficiency than a conventional surface-relief transmission grating with step shaped grooves, and broader spectral bandwidth than a volume phase holographic (VPH) grating. 　The trapezoid grating further improves the peak diffraction efficiency compared with the VB grating. 　The RFT grating is a novel transmission echelle grating which achieves both a higher diffraction efficiency and wider spectral bandwidth than conventional reflection echelle gratings. 　The prism-array enables us to reduce thickness of a grism along the optical axis and to increase its resolving power of the grism. 　The current status of development and initial performance of these gratings and prism arrays are presented.

Items.Authors: Riccardo Ferrazzoli, Enrico Costa, Sergio Fabiani, Philip Kaaret, Stephen L. O'Dell, Brian D. Ramsey, Paolo Soffitta, Luca Baldini, Ronaldo Bellazzini, Alessandro Di Marco, Fabio La Monaca, Luca Latronico, Alberto Manfreda, Fabio Muleri, John Rankin, Carmelo Sgrò, Stefano Silvestri, Martin C. Weisskopf
Items.Title: On-orbit imaging performance and stability of IXPE’s three X-ray telescopes
Items.Abstract: We report a 30-month on-orbit assessment of IXPE’s three X-ray telescopes.   By fitting a composite PSF to point-source data and comparing with ground calibrations, we find stable imaging performance with mean HPDs of $26.1''$, $32.1''$, and $30.9''$ for Telescopes 1–3, respectively.   No secular degradation is seen, and count-rate effects are negligible up to ~60 cts s⁻¹ (2–3 keV).   A 99% C.L. upper limit of 4.4% is placed on optics-induced polarization in the PSF halo; the modulation factor shows no wing-to-core degradation.   IXPE meets its ≤30″ requirement and remains well suited for spatially resolved X-ray polarimetry through 2030.

Items.Authors: Thomas R. Swindle, Zach Gazak, Eric Blackhurst, Kevin Iott, Justin Fletcher
Items.Title: On-sky performance of mobile, off-grid, robotic observatory for space domain awareness
Items.Abstract: Space domain awareness is a rapidly growing niche in ground- and space-based astronomy due in part to a 20-30% YOY growth in on-orbit population. The mere density of objects in space and the increased rate of events necessitates a larger, more rapidly responding network of sensors. In 2024, we presented the Deployable, Attritable Optical telescope as a solution concept. A collaboration between the US Space Force (USSF) and the commercial astronomy market, this mobile, off-grid, robotic observatory for space domain awareness (SDA) achieved first light in 2025 and now operates nightly at Siding Spring Observatory in Australia. We will review the design, which is now offered publicly through PlaneWave Instruments, its detection and orbit determination performance for satellites ranging from low-Earth to xGEO orbits, and demonstrate rapid follow-up of a space event through the USSF MACHINA program, an autonomous sensor orchestration agent for SDA presented separately in these proceedings.

Items.Authors: Joshua Oppor, Gary Hill, Hanshin Lee, Gregory Zeimann, Niv Drory, Maya Debski, Brian Vattiat, John Good, Jason Vestuto, Casey Kyte
Items.Title: On-sky performance testing of the VIRUS2 fiber-fed integral field spectrograph
Items.Abstract: We evaluate VIRUS2 performance during the first phase of commissioning involving 2 of 6 identical units. A single unit contains 256 fibers each subtending 2.5” which are split into 4 spectral channels covering 370-930 nm at R>2000. With 1536 total fibers, the complete IFU covers a footprint of 1.7’ x 1.3’ on the McDonald Observatory 2.7 m Harlan J. Smith Telescope. Using 1/3 of the final footprint, we present the first end-to-end performance tests with full capability. We discuss as-built detector statistics, fiber-to-fiber variations, and other instrument characteristics compared to specifications. Importantly, we evaluate the performance of the novel beam-switch module (BSM) and compare back-to-back observations of the same galaxy with its predecessor on the same telescope. Finally, we discuss the utility of VIRUS2 for studies of extended nearby galaxies like M31 where the combination of IFU footprint, spatial resolution, and spectral coverage is currently unprecedented.

Items.Authors: Andrew Ferayorni, Sarah Jaeggli
Items.Title: Operational Efficiency Improvements for the DL-NIRSP Instrument Control System
Items.Abstract: The National Science Foundation’s Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) is a 4-meter solar observatory in operation at Haleakalā, Hawaii. The Diffraction Limited Near Infrared Spectropolarimeter (DLNIRSP) is a key instrument at DKIST that measures magnetic fields and dynamics in the Sun's atmosphere. The DLNIRSP has a complex instrument control system with multiple camera and motion sub-systems that perform synchronized data acquisition sequences. Several improvements to the control system have been made recently to increase efficiency and reduce duty cycle. Optimizations in mechanism move times, field mapping patterns, and camera triggering schemes have yielded efficiency gains of up to 3X. In this paper we describe areas of the control system marked for improvement and different solutions considered. We review changes made to mechanism and camera timing and discuss how we verified our results. We conclude by discussing future optimizations that may improve efficiency further.

Items.Authors: Sasikan Suriyot, Weerapot Wanajaroen, Chanisa Kanjanasakul, Thierry Lepine, Sukrit Sucharitakul
Items.Title: Optical design and performance estimation of the 0.8 m Ritchey–Chrétien telescope for NARIT's public regional observatory
Items.Abstract: This work outlines the optical design for a 0.8-meter Ritchey-Chrétien telescope, a flagship instrument for a new regional observatory in Thailand developed by the National Astronomical Research Institute of Thailand (NARIT). The f/10 system features an 800 mm aperture and a wide 17 arcminute field of view. A Nasmyth focus enables rapid instrument switching. Comprehensive engineering analysis, including performance tolerancing and stray light mitigation, confirms the system's robustness, with a designed baffle system reducing stray light by an order of magnitude. This project serves as a foundational milestone, strategically building indigenous expertise to propel Thailand toward the future development of larger, more complex astronomical telescopes.

Items.Authors: Lixi Tang
Items.Title: Optical design of adaptive optics system for 600mm afocal telescope in long-baseline interferometric array
Items.Abstract: Long-baseline optical interferometry is achieved by combining multiple sub-telescopes into an equal large-aperture, high spatial resolution optical system. The wavefront quality of each sub-telescope will affect the contrast of the interference fringes. The optical design of the adaptive optics system for 600mm afocal telescopes presented. High speed deformable mirror and high sensitivity wavefront sensor are applied in our system to provide key devices for the adaptive optics system of the long-baseline interferometric telescope array under construction in China.

Items.Authors: Giorgio M. Pariani, Marco Bonaglia, Marco M. Riva, Andrea Di Rocco, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: Optical design of the MORFEO low order WFS atmospheric dispersion corrector
Items.Abstract: MORFEO, the Multi-Conjugated Adaptive Optics (MCAO) module for the ELT, is equipped with three Low Order and Reference (LOR) modules, implementing the Natural Guide Star wavefront sensing functionalities. In this paper, after a description of the overall optical design of the LOR module, we concentrate on the ADC design, which is incredibly demanding, both in terms of dispersion and pointing accuracy. We will present the methodology we used for the glass selection, performed with a Matlab-based routine at the maximum Zenith angle. The best solutions were then optimized in Zemax at all Zenith angles, and ranked by dispersion residuals, sensitivity to thermal variations, prisms’ apex angles, pupil wobbling and glass availability and price. For the best candidate, we evaluated the sensitivity to the atmospheric model, manufacturing errors and temperature variations, to provide the expected performances in terms of dispersion and pointing of the LO WFS module.

Items.Authors: Morgane Loquet Le Gall, Bruno Maffei, Créidhe O'Sullivan, Neal Trappe, Saoirse Doyle, Pierre Guiot
Items.Title: Optical development of the BISOU breadboard
Items.Abstract: BISOU (Balloon Interferometer for Spectral Observations of the primordial Universe) is an astronomical balloon-borne pathfinder developed as part of a preparatory study for a future space mission aimed at measuring spectral distortions of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). A laboratory breadboard of the instrument is being developed at the Institut d’Astrophysique Spatiale (IAS), enabling the characterization of subsystems and instrument systematic effects. The optical system is based on a differential polarizing Fourier Transform Spectrometer (FTS) that receives inputs from both a sky-facing telescope and an internal calibration source. The FTS focal planes include sub-K bolometric detectors coupled to multimode feed horns, with distinct focal planes dedicated to the low- and high-frequency bands covering the 90 - 1500 GHz range. The optical analysis first relies on ray-tracing simulations to establish the overall configuration of the system, be

Items.Authors: Carmelo Arcidiacono, Fernando Pedichini, Marco M. Riva, Gianluca Di Rico, Elisa Portaluri, Demetrio Magrin
Items.Title: Optical Heterodyne Long-Baseline Interferometry: a concept study of feasibility, photon budget, and science requirements
Items.Abstract: We explore the feasibility of Optical Heterodyne Long-Baseline Interferometry (OHLBI) for bright stellar and AGN science. Narrow-band heterodyne detection preserves phase beyond the atmospheric coherence time, enabling long integrations if photon-noise limits and Local Oscillator (LO) stability are controlled. Starting from the demonstrated performance of the Infrared Spatial Interferometer and earlier optical VLBI studies, we quantify expected SNR for key cases: surface imaging of bright O/B stars, time-resolved mapping of rapid rotators, eclipsing binaries, and kinematic studies of luminous AGN cores. We derive realistic photon budgets at visible and NIR wavelengths and identify regimes where heterodyne phase stability provides a scientific advantage over direct detection. We outline system requirements for a pathfinder, AO-fed receivers, comb-stabilized LOs and multi-site correlation, and define a roadmap toward future hybrid direct/heterodyne interferometry.

Items.Authors: Lixin Zheng, Chun Xu, Zhenya Zheng, Kexin Li, Dan Zhou
Items.Title: Optical metrology of the filters for the Multi-Channel Imager of the CSST
Items.Abstract: The Multi-Channel Imager (MCI) is a panchromatic imager that will be deployed in the China Space Station Telescope. It is a powerful near-ultraviolet (NUV) and visible imager on CSST, with a wavelength coverage spanning 255nm to 1000 nm. The MCI high sensitivity, high spatial resolution, and. large field-of-view (FOV) will provide the astronomer with a set of tools for astrophysical. The MCI consists of three imaging channels, which are the NUV channel, the Optical-blue channel and the Optical-red channel, each with its own complement of filters. Each channel of the MCI uses a 9kx9k e2v CCD to cover a 7.5′×7.5′ field of view (FOV). The filter complement, which includes broad, medium, and narrow band filters, naturally reflects the diversity of astronomical programs to be targeted with MCI.

Items.Authors: Masaki Ito, Takumi Ogawa, Hirotaka Kondo, Satoshi Ikari, Taro Matsuo, Ryu Funase, Shinichi Nakasuka
Items.Title: Optical path difference control method for SEIRIOS mission and its applicability to future formation flying space-based interferometers
Items.Abstract: SEIRIOS is a formation flying micro-satellite mission for infrared interferometric observations using a densified pupil spectrograph. To obtain clear interference fringes, extremely strict optical path difference (OPD) control is required.  In this presentation, we propose a novel method that estimates the OPD from interference fringe images obtained by a densified pupil spectrograph and feeds it back to onboard actuators such as delay-line stages and tip–tilt mirrors. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through ground-based experiments and numerical simulations, showing that sub-micrometer-level OPD estimation and control can be achieved from a single image. Furthermore, by presenting the current OPD control sequence in the SEIRIOS mission, we demonstrate that the proposed method provides a highly promising approach for future OPD control in formation flying space-based interferometers.

Items.Authors: Qian Chen, Xufang Li
Items.Title: Optical performance of the AliCPT-1 Telescope
Items.Abstract: Ali CMB Polarization Telescope (AliCPT) is a 72 cm on-axis retracting telescope located at an altitude of 5250 m in Ali (Nagri) area of Tibet, China. It is the first project in the northern hemisphere designed for CMB polarization observation. The first state of AliCPT (AliCPT-1) has been deployed in April, 2025. AliCPT-1 has about 1700 transition edge sensor bolometers and supports observation capabilities at 90 GHz and 150 GHz. This presentation will report the performance of AliCPT-1. We present results from calibration campaign in situ at Ali, including detector spectral response, optical efficiency, near-field beam (NFBM), far-field beam (FFBM) and far-side lobe (FSLM).

Items.Authors: Yoko Tanaka, Yosuke Minowa, Nick Herrald, Noelia Martínez Rey, Hajime Ogane, Yoshito Ono, Koki Terao
Items.Title: Optical performance verification of the ULTIMATE-Subaru wavefront sensor subsystem
Items.Abstract: The ULTIMATE-Subaru project is developing a new Ground Layer Adaptive Optics (GLAO) system for the Subaru Telescope to improve image quality over a wide 14×14 arcminute field of view. The system uses four Laser Guide Stars (LGS) and four Natural Guide Stars (NGS), observed by a series of eight Wavefront Sensors (WFSs). A dedicated light source, called Star Simulator, is designed to help align and calibrate the WFSs. The WFS system and Star Simulator are currently in the final design phase. The optics for the NGS WFS, LGS WFS, and Star Simulator were procured for prototyping test purposes. These optical components such as relay optics, lens arrays, and subassemblies combining Star Simulator, collimator, and camera optics were evaluated by measuring the wavefront errors. The test results show the system meets their performance requirements. This paper summarizes the test procedures and their results confirming the readiness for final assembly.

Items.Authors: Yunfen Dong, Yiding Ping
Items.Title: Optical system design for the 2.5-meter multi-purpose Universal Telescope
Items.Abstract: This paper discusses the challenges and design trade-offs for the optical system of the 2.5-meter Multi-Target General-purpose Telescope, which aims to simultaneously achieve high-precision astrometry of solar system objects and lunar laser ranging. The telescope must deliver the ultra-high imaging quality and positional accuracy required for astrometry, alongside the key performance metrics essential for laser ranging, such as a shared transmit/receive optical path, high energy efficiency, extremely low wavefront distortion, and a high signal-to-noise ratio. The study indicates that selecting the optical configuration and determining the complexity of the mirror surfaces are central to balancing imaging performance, ranging capability, engineering feasibility, and manufacturing cost.

Items.Authors: Anna Rose Polish
Items.Title: Optics and broadband anti-reflection coatings for the BA4-90/150 receiver
Items.Abstract: The BICEP Array telescopes search for primordial B-mode polarization from inflationary gravitational waves. This signal is exceedingly faint, demanding excellent map depth and systematics control. The new BA4-90/150 receiver introduces a wide 77–169 GHz dichroic band, requiring upgrades throughout the optics chain to reduce loss, reflections, and thermal loading. We developed improved anti-reflection coatings for the HMPE window, HDPE lenses, and nylon infrared filter, extending previous technology to span more than an octave of bandwidth. The thermal filtering scheme and several mechanical elements were also updated to further suppress optical loss, reflections, and beam truncation. We summarize the updated optical design, material choices, expected thermal and spectral performance, and laboratory results from coated prototypes. These results establish the readiness of the optics and AR-coating approach for BA4-90/150 and provide a foundation for future wide-band CMB instruments.

Items.Authors: Fabrice Madec, Johan Floriot, Tony Pamplona, William Bon, Térence Baugé, Remi Lamble, Michael carle, Basile Fayol, Alexia Odievre, Christophe Fabron, Anne Costille, Laure Ciesla, Denis Burgarella
Items.Title: Opto-mechanical design for PRIMAger instrument of the PRIMA mission
Items.Abstract: PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics (PRIMA), is an infrared observatory for the next decade, with a 1.8 m telescope actively cooled to 4.5 K, currently in mission concept study of Probe Explorers part of Explorer Program.  PRIMAger, one of two instruments, will provide two channels, hyperspectral from 24 to 84 μm with a spectral resolution R ≥ 8 and polarimetric from 80 to 264 μm.  The Laboratoire d’Astrophysique de Marseille is in charge of the system engineering, of the delivery of the opto-mechanical assembly as well as the integration of the instrument. In this paper we will describe the opto-mechanical design based on off-axis freeform Aluminium mirrors. The mechanical design will be also presented including the carbon fiber bi-pods that allow to maintain and thermally isolate the 1K structure from the 4.5K metering payload structure.  We will present the development plan strategy as well as the overall verification strategy especially the optical alignment and tests.

Items.Authors: Xuhao Wu, Dehua Yang, Fanghua Jiang
Items.Title: Optomechanical design of SH wavefront sensor for the wide field focus of the JUST Telescope
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the optomechanical design of a Shack-Hartmann (SH) wavefront sensor for the wide-field focus of the Shanghai Jiao Tong University Spectral Telescope (JUST). The design addresses the specific requirements for precision wavefront sensing in JUST's wide-field optical system. Key considerations include the mechanical mounting and alignment of the lenslet array relative to the telescope's focal plane, the structural stability under varying operational conditions, and the integration with existing optical interfaces. The proposed design ensures robust mechanical support, precise positional control, and minimal thermal deformation, thereby maintaining the high optical fidelity required for accurate wavefront measurement. This sensor is crucial for the active alignment and performance optimization of the JUST.

Items.Authors: Mathieu Motte, Vincent Chambouleyron, Romain Fétick, Mary Angelie Alagao, Eduard Muslimov, Arnaud Striffling, Mahawa Cissé, Benoît Neichel, Thierry Fusco, Jean-François Sauvage, Cédric Taïssir Héritier, Francisco Oyarzun, Edvardas Vinerskas, Mattéo Pasinetti, Sylvain Cetre, François Huppert, Marc Ferrari
Items.Title: PAPYRUS @ OHP: a second adaptive optics stage with a vector Zernike wavefront sensor for PAPYRUS at the Observatoire de Haute Provence
Items.Abstract: Characterising Earth-like exoplanets from ground-based telescopes requires reaching high contrast and hence the use of an extreme adaptive optics (AO) system. In such systems, temporal error is the main contributor to the error budget. One way to reduce it is to make the control loop run faster. This implies a drop in photons per frame, and, consequently, in SNR on the wavefront sensor (WFS) camera. Using more sensitive WFSs is therefore required, but their limited dynamic range makes it challenging to correct atmospheric turbulence. A solution is to deploy them in a second AO stage to correct low-order residuals from the first stage.   To test such concepts, we added a second stage based on a vector Zernike WFS on PAPYRUS which significantly improved its on-sky performance. We will present the bench and its performance as compared to simulations, and summarise the lessons learnt for the development of future XAO instruments.

Items.Authors: Enrico Biancalani, Eduardo Bendek, Kevin Wagner, Edward Balaban
Items.Title: Pathways to exo-world discovery with fluidic space-assembled telescopes
Items.Abstract: In-space assembly of mirrors via the scale-invariant technology of fluidic shaping can enable the paradigm shift from space-borne to space-assembled telescopes, to be iteratively scaled up at a lower cost. Starting from a minimal pathfinder fluidic telescope, we explore some of the potential exo-world science cases made observationally accessible by larger architectures. In particular, we propose to study the feasibility of a dedicated fluidic telescope with an aperture of 3+ m---having assessed the detection limits of the Roman Space Telescope---to conduct a relative-astrometry monitoring campaign on the directly-imaged habitable-zone giant exoplanet candidate α Centauri Ab, in search of Earth-like exomoons. Then, we review the possible discovery and characterization returns of follow-up missions to the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO): from variations on the Large UV/Optical/IR Surveyor (LUVOIR) concept to even larger fluidic-telescope architectures.
